perspective:
**Sara’s available information:**

- Sara knows she is a Speech-Language Pathologist and American Indian. She has worked for several years at a community health center with Shirley Whiteplume, a nurse, and considers Shirley a long-time colleague and close friend.
- Sara knows a mutual patient died and she attended his funeral.
- At the funeral, Sara observed Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. Sara heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking something more could have been done. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy they brought. She heard Shirley agree but say it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara raised their treatment decisions and said she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley told Sara she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- Sara observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet office moment, Sara told Shirley she had noticed she was holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Shirley said she wasn’t sure she could and didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions isn’t weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara felt she might have come on too strong and apologized. Shirley told her it was a bit much but that she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said continuing to talk helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better and felt hopeful. She asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that and suggested planning something for the weekend.
